title: The Chaldeans
lead: The Chaldeans (Hebrew Kasdim) were a people of southern Babylonia whose dynasty, begun by Nabopolassar in 626 BC and carried on by Nebuchadnezzar, ruled Babylon and destroyed Jerusalem in 586 BC. In Daniel the word also names a learned class.

sections.b: The Chaldeans appear as the Babylonian army in Kings, Jeremiah, Habakkuk and Ezekiel (2 Kings 24-25; Jeremiah 21; Habakkuk 1:6; Ezekiel 23:14-15), as the home of Abraham's family in Ur of the Chaldeans (Genesis 11:28, a later name for the region), and as a class of wise men in Daniel (Daniel 1:4; 2:2). Habakkuk gives the fullest portrait of their army (1:6-11).
sections.refs: 2 Kings 24:1-2; 2 Kings 25:4-10; Genesis 11:28; Habakkuk 1:6-11; Daniel 1:4; Daniel 2:2
